learning_objective: 🎯 Master the math of electrons! Understand current, voltage, and resistance, and learn how circuits power everything in our modern world.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Current ($$I$$) is the rate of flow of electric charge (electrons). Measured in Amperes (A). Potential Difference or Voltage ($$V$$) is the 'push' that makes charges move. Measured in Volts (V).

The most important rule in electricity! It states that the voltage across a conductor is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided temperature remains constant. Formula: $$V = I \times R$$.

Resistance ($$R$$) opposes the flow of current. It depends on the length of the wire (longer = more resistance), area of cross-section (thicker = less resistance), and the material (Resistivity, $$\rho$$).

In Series, resistors are connected end-to-end ($$R_s = R_1 + R_2$$). If one breaks, the whole circuit stops. In Parallel, resistors are connected across the same two points ($$\frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2}$$). Domestic circuits are in parallel so devices work independently.

When current flows through a high-resistance wire, it generates heat (Joule's Law of Heating: $$H = I^2Rt$$). Electric Power ($$P$$) is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed: $$P = VI = I^2R = \frac{V^2}{R}$$.

fun_activity.title: 🔌 The Lemon Battery
fun_activity.instructions: Roll a juicy lemon to soften it. Insert a galvanized (zinc) nail and a copper coin into the lemon without them touching. If you connect them to a digital voltmeter, you will see a small voltage! The lemon acid acts as an electrolyte.

exam_tips: 📌 Ammeter is always connected in series, and Voltmeter is always connected in parallel.
📌 Always write SI units in numerical answers: Current (A), Voltage (V), Resistance (Ω), Power (W), Energy (J).
📌 1 Commercial unit of electrical energy (1 kWh) = $$3.6 \times 10^6$$ Joules.
quick_recap: ⭐ The direction of conventional current is opposite to the flow of electrons.
⭐ Tungsten is used for bulb filaments because it has a very high melting point and high resistivity.
⭐ Fuses are safety devices based on the heating effect of electric current.
